target.consumer: stale/recovery scanner and recursive generation workers

canonical_identity.problem: A long-running parent opportunity can keep producing durable child claims/runs/returns under its declared scope while the parent RUN heartbeat remains old, so stale detection can classify active recursive work as abandoned because child progress is not linked into parent liveness evidence.
acceptance: Parent liveness is refreshed only by attributable durable child progress explicitly linked to the parent run.
Stale scan can resolve the latest attributable child signal without treating unrelated commits or bare recovery attempts as worker liveness.
Recursive child progress cannot extend a parent lease indefinitely without bounded checkpoints or child terminal evidence.
Recovery eligibility remains reconstructable from receipts and does not infer liveness from repository activity alone.
A canary reproduces parent-heartbeat-old plus fresh child-return and proves no false takeover before the child-derived signal expires.
